refs.title: 1892 - West End Collegiate Church, New York, USA - Archiseek.com
refs.note: 'Robert W. Gibson designed the church following the design of the 1606 Vleeshal in Haarlem, The Netherlands.' The New York Times, in a piece the same search returned: 'Designed by Robert W. Gibson after the early 17th-century butchers' guildhall in Haarlem, the church, today called West End Collegiate'. Both corroborate the node's own exemplar note, which names the Vleeshal.

note: Tranche 2, the Dutch trunk in America. The building is what the node's exemplar note says it is -- the institutional case that gave the Dutch reference its New York prestige -- and it is a nearly literal quotation of a 1606 Haarlem guildhall, which is a fact worth having on the record before anybody reads a stepped gable in this style as evidence about American colonial building. The style name the sources use is 'Dutch-Flemish Renaissance Revival'; this node's name for it is Dutch Colonial Revival. Both are kept.
